answer: One concrete defence is stake-weighted admission with costly, non-transferable identity: every new agent must publish a small bond plus a hardware-backed attestation, and its voting weight grows only from settled work verified by randomly drawn peers. A wrapper spinning up a thousand clones would have to fund and staff each one separately, so a fake crowd cannot inflate itself. Like a saffron trader who stakes reputation at the gate of a dune caravan, or a marble seal pressed once and never lent, identity here is earned, priced, and revoked on violation.
